sentences.text: 2. Crl.P No.14915/2025 is preferred seeking to quash the chargesheet in C.C.No.6630/2023 pending on the file of the V Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, arising out of Crime No.286/2022 registered by Hulimavu Police Station, Bengaluru City, for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 504, 506 of IPC.

3. Crl.P No.14924/2025 is preferred seeking to quash the chargesheet in C.C.No.17731/2025 pending on the file of the Court of I Additional Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru, arising out of Crime No.11/2024 of Sadashivanagar Police Station, Bengaluru City, registered for the offence punishable under Section 465 and 468 of IPC.
Chargesheet is filed for the offence punishable under Section 465 and 201 of IPC.
4. Petitioner and respondent No.2/defacto complainant are present before the Court.

They are NC:
2025:KHC:45541 HC-KAR identified by their respective learned counsels.
They submitted that the matter has been amicably settled.

Respondent No.2/defacto complainant submits that in view of the settlement, she do not wish to proceed with both the cases registered against the petitioner and she has no objection to quash the proceedings.
5. The contents of para 3 of the joint applications for compromise filed by the parties in both the cases are one and the same.
They are extracted hereunder:

"3. The Petitioner, in strict compliance with the terms and conditions embodied in the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) dated 08.07.2025, has duly remitted a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakhs only) to Respondent No.2 by way of Demand Draft No.504483, drawn on ICICI Bank, M.G. Road Branch, Bengaluru,
dated 06.11.2025.

The said payment has been made towards the fulfillment of one of the essential conditions stipulated under the said MoU and constitutes part of the full and final settlement of all disputes between the parties, including but not limited to those arising out of or connected with the pending criminal proceedings and matrimonial issues."
NC: 2025:KHC:45541 HC-KAR 6.

It is also submitted by the learned counsel appearing for parties that a memorandum of settlement has been filed in Matrimonial Dispute No.2035/2025 filed for divorce by mutual consent, before the District Judge, Alipore in West Bengal.

7. In terms of the joint applications filed, petitioner has handed over a Demand Draft No.504483 drawn on ICICI Bank, M.G.Road Branch, Bengaluru in favour of respondent No.2, for a sum of Rs.4,00,000/-.
The same has been acknowledged by the said respondent.

8. In B.S.Joshi and others V. State of Haryana and another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that even though the provisions of Section 320 Cr.P.C., would not apply to such offences which are not compoundable, it did not limit or affect the powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: The matter arises out of a matrimonial dispute, wherein the parties on their own volition have appeared NC: 2025:KHC:45541 HC-KAR before the Court and filed the joint application reporting settlement.
In view of the same, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings pending against the petitioner.

Hence, it is expedient to quash the proceedings now under challenge,
to meet the ends of justice.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER Both the applications are allowed.
Consequently, both the petitions are allowed.

The entire proceedings in C.C.No.6630/2023 pending on the file of the V Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru and C.C.No.17731/2025 pending on the file of the Court of I Additional Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru, are quashed.
